items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1962-08-26
items.q: I heard from Snoozer Quinn way before I ever met Jack Teagarden.

ctx.x: That's the truth of it. And Snoozer, oh, I want to tell you this. Snoozer was the creator of the style that Jack Teagarden sings. The first I ever heard of that style of singing, which is marvelous, I heard from Snoozer Quinn way before I ever met Jack Teagarden.

items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: some of the choruses that Jack Teagard plays, which were taken verbatim from Peck Kelly

ctx.x: over. We'll be back right after this. there's a very, very interesting story behind Snoozer Quinn's rendition, and that was Snoozer's Wanderings. And I want Mr. Johnny Wiggs to tell us just how that record was recorded. Well, I hope we have time to start at the beginning. I met Snoozer when Peck Kelly sent for me. Peck Kelly was considered one of the greatest piano players that ever lived. And he was playing in Freeport, and they sent for me, and I pulled out my horn to play the dinner session. And it was a big band in those days. That was supposed…

slam the door in nurses' faces. It was done out at the hospital, the TB hospital out the lake. I had to slam the door in audits' faces. I had to take phones off of hooks and brush off the hair which is caused by these platter machines. And lo and behold, if we didn't get 12 of fairly good sides, which are on the market now. Okay, and we're going to be hearing some of those, but first we have to bring you this message. Hi, Karate, after Shaven. Cologne presents. All right, we want to wish a very happy birthday…
